Avery — thanks for the summary and the questionnaire. Initial take from Commercial:

- Net 45: acceptable for this customer, want to lock a late-payment interest clause and a credit hold trigger at 60+ days.
- Activation fee: prefer 25% in signings for smaller pilots; however, if we can mitigate risk (PO in-hand, initial usage commit) we can consider 10%.
- Invoice split: OK in principle but need explicit order form appendix that maps POs to line items/entities and clarifies tax responsibility per invoice.
- Tax: we need evidence for reverse-charge (EU) and the customer's completed Tax_Classification_Questionnaire. We cannot proactively accept withholding responsibility — customer must provide W-8/W-9 or equivalent.

I'll draft amendment language for the order form appendix and a short clause for tax & invoicing. Looping in Lauren to propose exact payment language and Karthik for accounting handoff.

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposed order-form snippets for PulseWave invoicing / tax

Team — suggested redline snippets below (short and actionable so procurement can accept without Legal-heavy edits):

1) Payment terms (Order Form Appendix):
"Payment Terms: Unless otherwise stated in the Order Form Appendix, Customer shall pay invoices within thirty (30) days of invoice date. For this Order Form, parties agree Net 45. Late payments will incur interest at 1.5% per month or the maximum allowed by law. Redwood may suspend service after 60 days delinquent following written notice."

2) Activation fee & invoice cadence:
"Activation Fee: Customer shall pay an activation fee equal to 25% of the first period's fees within fifteen (15) days of execution. Remaining fees will be invoiced monthly in arrears. If Customer provides a PO and confirms approval for 10% activation instead of 25%, the Parties will reflect that election in the Order Form Appendix at signing."

3) Multi-entity invoicing & tax responsibility:
"Invoice Routing: Customer may supply entity-specific POs. Redwood will invoice the entity indicated on each PO. Customer is responsible for applicable VAT, withholding taxes, and for providing tax residency documentation (W-9, W-8BEN-E, VAT ID). Where applicable, Customer shall provide documented evidence supporting reverse-charge treatment prior to Redwood issuing VAT-exempt invoices."

If that looks good, Avery, send to PulseWave as a compact 'commercial compromise' note. I can hand off to Legal if they push further.

Lauren Bishop
Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference

Matt — thanks for the redlines. Quick summary of what we can propose back as a short compromise to keep this moving:

- Net terms: Accept Net 45 for this Order Form. Redwood will include late interest and a 60-day credit-hold suspension clause.
- Activation fee: We prefer 25% but will accept 10% if PulseWave confirms a PO up front and signs the Order Form appendix reflecting 10%.
- Invoice split: PulseWave can submit separate POs per entity. Redwood will invoice the entity specified on the PO and issue VAT invoices where applicable. Customer must submit the completed Tax_Classification_Questionnaire (attached) and any W-9/W-8 documentation.
- Tax: If PulseWave requires reverse-charge handling for EU entities, provide VAT ID and evidence. Redwood will issue VAT invoices or cooperate to support reverse-charge once documentation is received.

Next steps:
1) Matt — confirm whether PulseWave will issue a PO on execution and whether you can accept the 10% activation fee with PO in-hand.
2) If yes, I will update the Order Form appendix with Lauren's language and route through DocuSign (link below).
3) Please return the completed Tax_Classification_Questionnaire and W-9/W-8 if relevant.
